# #667 — lane-bootstrap: add continuation mode for existing branches (ledger 30.2)

Operator ruling 2026-08-08 (ledger item 30.2). scripts/lane-bootstrap.ts hard-codes `git worktree add -b <branch> <path> origin/main` (lines ~302-309) and fatals when the branch already exists, so every continuation lane hand-replicates fetch / worktree-add-without--b / .env copy / bun install — the exact hand-building ledger item 15 exists to stop (round 21 Tightening records the interim recipe).

Wanted: a continuation path — when the named branch exists, add the worktree WITHOUT -b, verify the local branch tip matches origin (refuse loudly on divergence, naming both SHAs — never silently reset), then the same .env copy and frozen-lockfile install. The existing fresh-branch path and the leftover-worktree refusal are unchanged. Scope note: ledger 15's teardown rejection stands — this is bootstrap-side only, no teardown automation.

Done-means (red-first): (a) continuation on an existing in-sync branch succeeds and the worktree is on that branch at the right SHA (RED today: the script fatals); (b) control — fresh-branch path unchanged; (c) divergent local-vs-origin branch is REFUSED with both SHAs named (negative control: inject divergence, confirm refusal — and the refusal must happen BEFORE any worktree is created, plant-and-survive style); (d) leftover-worktree refusal unchanged. Announce rule: any state the script inspects and declines to touch is named in output.

Fast-lane eligible: known class (bootstrap tooling, purpose-built check pattern at scripts/done-means/659/661), bounded diff.

### Direction taken and why — PR #669 body

> ## Summary
>
> - Fixes #667. `scripts/lane-bootstrap.ts` hard-coded `git worktree add -b <branch> <path> origin/main`. `-b` means CREATE, so the script fatalled the moment the named branch already existed, and every continuation lane hand-replicated fetch / worktree-add-without-`-b` / `.env` copy / frozen-lockfile install — the hand-building ledger item 15 exists to stop (ledger item 30.2; round 21 Tightening recorded the interim recipe as a known tax).
> - When the branch already exists, the script now resolves the local tip and `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>`, and checks the branch out **where it already points**, without `-b`.
> - **Divergence is refused before anything is created**, naming both SHAs. A refusal that does not say what to reconcile is a dead end (round 15's dead-end-error class), and a silent reset would discard a lane's own work — so the script never resets, forces, or discards to make a bootstrap succeed.
> - A local-only branch (no origin counterpart) is continued and **named as such** — it is not divergence, but "nothing is pushed, this lane is the only copy" is worth the operator knowing.
> - Unchanged by design: the fresh-branch path, the leftover-worktree refusal, and teardown staying printed-never-executed. Ledger item 15's teardown rejection still stands — this is bootstrap-side only, and no code path here removes, resets, or moves a ref.
> - Announce rule (AGENTS.md "nothing is adjusted silently"): every inspected-but-untouched state is named — which path ran, the verified sync SHA, and that the branch ref was not touched. The `LANE READY` summary now reports the real starting point instead of always printing "from origin/main".
>

> ## Critical Self-Review
>
> - Highest-risk behavior: checking out an existing branch without `-b`. The failure that would matter is continuing onto a branch whose local state does not match what the lane expects — which is exactly why divergence refuses rather than reconciling, and why clause (a) asserts the worktree HEAD equals the existing branch tip and is **not** origin/main. A naive branch-name-only assertion would pass for a silent re-cut.
> - Assumptions that could be wrong: (1) that `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` is fresh enough to compare against — the script fetches immediately before, but a branch pushed by another machine between fetch and compare would be judged on a stale ref; the refusal is the safe direction there. (2) That a local-only branch should continue rather than refuse. I chose continue-and-announce because a lane that has not pushed yet is the ordinary continuation case; refusing it would reintroduce the hand-build. Flagged as a judgment call, not a ruling.
> - Missing/weak tests: the check never exercises a real network fetch (see the announced fixture adjustment) — a defect in fetch itself would be outside its vantage. The `--fresh-db` path is not re-tested against continuation; it is orthogonal to the branch decision and `lane-bootstrap-known-good.sh` clause 3 still covers it.
> - Security/permission risk: none. No auth, namespace, SQL, or network-mutating path is touched. The only new git operations are `show-ref`, `rev-parse`, and `worktree add` without `-b`.
> - Migration/deploy risk: none. Developer tooling only; no schema, no serving code, nothing deployed.
> - Downstream client/runtime risk: none. `scripts/lane-bootstrap.ts` is not imported by the server, the Python client, or any MCP surface; it has no consumers outside lane setup in this repo.
> - Rollback/cleanup concern: reverting the commit restores the exact prior `worktree add -b` behavior; there is no state to migrate back. The check creates only RUN_ID-carrying branches and worktrees and refuses to remove any name lacking that RUN_ID.
> - Fixes made before PR: (1) the clause (e) false-positive described above, caught by reading WHY each RED clause failed rather than the tally (round 18) — a bare substring matched git's fatal and would have banked a green on a crashing script; (2) the `LANE READY` summary still printed "(from origin/main)" over a continuation, misstating the lane's own starting point, so it now reports the path that actually ran.
> - Known residual risk: the announce assertions in clause (e) match on the step text (`continuation`, `in sync`). Rewording those step messages without updating the check would regress the clause to passing for the wrong reason. No test enforces that coupling; the clause's evidence string naming each flag is the mitigation.

Named for that harvest: (1) a negative-match clause on a crashing subject can go green off the SUBJECT'S OWN error text — anchor announce-assertions on a marker the script owns, not on prose the failure mode also emits; (2) a summary line that hardcodes one path's provenance silently misreports the other once a second path exists.
